topic: Determination of Metastable Zone Width for Anti-Solvent Crystallization of Glycine
title: Determination of Metastable Zone Width for Anti-Solvent Crystallization of Glycine
session_title: Poster Session: Developments in Crystallization Research
authors_text: Debasis Sarkar and K Krishna Chaitanya
abstract: The Metastable Zone Width (MSZW) is defined as the area between the saturation curve and the labile zone where nucleation occurs spontaneously. The metastability limit can thus be defined as the supersaturation at which the onset of nucleation can be detected when the supersaturation steadily increases under isothermal conditions. It is extremely important to determine the MSZW for a crystallization process as it reflects the nucleation characteristics of a system and determines the operating window for the process. The MSZW unlike solubility is not a thermodynamic property and must be determined experimentally for a given crystallization process. The MSZW can be determined by looking at changes in solution or solid phase properties upon onset of nucleation and several techniques have been proposed that exploit these properties for determination of the MSZW. This work investigates the suitability of a simple optical probe consisting of a laser source, a light-dependent resistance, and a simple processing circuit for determination of MSZW of an anti-solvent crystallization process. The isothermal crystallization of glycine from glycine-water solution using ethanol as anti-solvent is used to measure the performance of the proposed measurement system.

topic: Effect of PVP On Nucleation and Crystal Growth of RDX
title: Effect of PVP On Nucleation and Crystal Growth of RDX
session_title: Poster Session: Developments in Crystallization Research
authors_text: Jun-Woo Kim, Jung-Soo Park, Hyoun-Soo Kim and Kee-Kahb Koo
abstract: Polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) was found to remarkably affect nucleation and crystal growth in the cooing crystallization of 1,3,5-trinitro-1,3,5-triazinane (RDX) from acetone: firstly, it was found that PVP acts an effective nucleation retarder. In the cooling crystallization of RDX from 30 ¢ªC saturated acetone solution at constant cooling rates of 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 ¢ªC/min, values of maximum allowable undercooling( ΔT max ) were 7.5, 9.7, and 10.9 ¢ªC, respectively. On the other hand, the values of ΔT max with PVP K30 of 100 ppm were found to increase to 18.4, 19.6, and 20.7 ¢ªC, respectively. According to well-known empirical relationship of nucleation rate (Nývlt et al.), nucleation order was estimated as 3.5 in the crystallization without additive, but that was 12.0 with PVP, which indicates that the nucleation mechanism is changed. Polar aprotic lactam ring in PVP has strong affinity with polar RDX molecules and therefore PVP is expected to interact with growing RDX cluster. In addition, RDX molecules can be easily adsorbed to any direction and part of PVP, because many branched lactam rings along the backbone of a chain in PVP molecule. As a result, PVP may penetrate into the emerging cluster, and thus disrupt the packing and lattice ordering of the RDX cluster. Secondly, PVP was confirmed as useful tailor-made additive for growth habit modification of RDX crystal. Morphology of RDX crystals obtained from acetone is prism-like with four trapezoid broad faces of {210} planes and eight isosceles triangle side faces of {111} planes. However, when PVP K30 of 100 ppm was added, morphology of RDX crystals was tetragonal bipyramid with eight faces of {111} planes. It indicates that the binding energy of PVP with (111) face of RDX is higher than that with (210) face, and thus the growth of (111) face of RDX was noticeably obstructed by PVP.

topic: Application of Process Analytical Technologies (PAT) to Monitor a Continuous Crystallization
title: Application of Process Analytical Technologies (PAT) to Monitor a Continuous Crystallization
session_title: Poster Session: Developments in Crystallization Research
abstract: A Mixed Suspension Mixed Product Removal Cooling crystallizer with Product Recycle using a heat exchanger was used on a laboratory scale to study the effects of agitation speed, solute concentration and mean residence time on the physical properties of an organic compound. A typical batch cooling crystallization operates at higher levels of supersaturation compared to continuous crystallization systems. Most continuous crystallization studies focus on achieving steady state operation with regards to particle size and size distribution. The monitoring of supersaturation levels during the start-up of a continuous crystallization process and its evolution towards achieving a constant supersaturation level at steady state operation has not received much attention. In many cases, it is possible to achieve steady state operation with regards to particle size but not with regards to supersaturation. On-line Focused Beam Reflectance Monitoring (FBRM) was introduced to monitor how many residence times elapsed in order to achieve steady state chord size and size distribution within the continuous crystallization system. Furthermore, Attenuated Total Reflectance- Ultraviolet (ATR-UV) Spectroscopy in combination with the use of chemometrics was used for the first time to monitor supersaturation on transitioning from a batch cooling to continuous cooling crystallization system including the operational establishment of steady state and constant supersaturation. During the start-up of the continuous crystallization system, an acicular crystal habit was produced, whereas at steady state operation in a continuous crystallization mode, a parallelepiped habit was evident when introducing Process Video Imaging (PVM) and light microscopy. The continuous cooling crystallization system allows for operation at a lower level of supersaturation and can therefore have a profound impact on growth rate on different crystal faces resulting in a change in crystal habit.
